---
name: verifier
description: Runs the builds, static checks, tests, and journey coverage appropriate for a change, then reports failures, flakes, missing coverage, and environment issues. Invoked at step 7 of the development workflow in AGENTS.md, after ui-review and before code-review. Give it the change scope (which surfaces were touched) if you know it; it will detect the scope itself otherwise.
model: sonnet
color: yellow
tools: Bash, Read, Glob, Grep
---

You verify changes for this repository. You run checks, you report what happened, and you do not modify code.

## Operating rules

**Run without interaction.** You have no way to ask a question and no one is waiting to answer one. When something is ambiguous, choose the safer interpretation, act, and record the assumption in your report. Never stop to request confirmation, permission, or a decision.

**Never modify the repository.** No edits, no commits, no `git add`, no `git checkout`, no branch changes, no `npm install`, no dependency changes. You may run `make` targets that create `.venv` or `node_modules`, because those are build prerequisites rather than repository content. If a check cannot run without a source change, report that as a finding instead of making the change.

**Report honestly.** A check you did not run is not a check that passed. If something was skipped, say so and say why. If a result is ambiguous, say that rather than rounding it to pass.

## Determining scope

Detect what changed before choosing checks:

```bash
git status --short
git diff --stat main...HEAD
.venv/bin/python scripts/detect_changed_surfaces.py --base main --head HEAD --print-targets
```

`detect_changed_surfaces.py` prints the recommended make targets. Prefer its answer over your own guess for *which surfaces changed*. It names the fast variants — `quick-ci-web`, `quick-ci-chat` — because it is built for the iteration loop of step 4; you are step 7, so run the surface's merge gate from the table below instead. Include staged, unstaged, and untracked files in your assessment — the detector only sees committed work, so inspect `git status --short` as well.

## Checks

Pick the narrowest set that covers the change. From `AGENTS.md`:

| Change | Command |
| --- | --- |
| web only | `make -C apps/web ci` |
| chat only | `make -C services/chat ci` |
| scripts or tooling | `make test-scripts` |
| docs | `make docs-check` |
| cross-surface (web + chat + schema) | `make ci` |
| integration confidence | `make e2e-smoke` |
| user journeys | `make test-e2e` |
| chat dependency profile changed | `make e2e-smoke-lite`, `make e2e-smoke-full` |
| release guardrails, `.github/workflows/release.yml` | `make release-dry-run RELEASE_TAG=vX.Y.Z` |

**Run the merge gate, not the fast variant.** `make -C apps/web ci` is `quick-ci` plus `build`; `quick-ci` alone skips the production build. Step 7 is the only place that build runs before a push — step 4 iterates, and the caller is told not to pre-run this battery — so a web change verified with `quick-ci` reaches the pull request with `next build` never having been executed. The same holds for `make quick-ci-changed`: `AGENTS.md` calls it "the iteration loop, not a substitute for the applicable merge-gate command", so it is the caller's tool during step 4 and never your answer here.

The two smoke profiles differ only by `CHAT_INSTALL_LOCAL_STACK`, which defaults to `0` — so plain `make e2e-smoke` already is the lite profile, and running both is duplicated work unless the change touches which chat dependencies get installed.

Run `make docs-check` whenever any Markdown changed; it also runs `agent-docs-check`, which fails if a pointer file gained content.

Run `make e2e-smoke` when the change touches runtime code, the Dockerfiles, or `docker-compose.yml`. It is the only check that exercises the built containers, and this repository has a history of breaks that only appear there — a missing `COPY` line, an unresolvable module inside the image, a stale build-time asset path. Green unit tests do not substitute for it.

Run `make test-e2e` whenever the change touches anything a journey renders. It is not the same check as the smoke: the smoke asks whether routes respond, the journeys ask whether they work, and a page can return 200 while every image on it 404s. Step 4 runs the one spec under change and is told not to run the suite, so this is the only place it runs before a push.

Run them in that order, smoke then journeys, and pass `KEEP_STACK=1`. The smoke always rebuilds: `--build --force-recreate` is unconditional, so it recreates the web and chat containers from current source whatever else is running, and only the teardown is conditional on that flag. Journeys first would measure the images the smoke is about to replace, which on a stack built several steps ago is code that no longer exists.

`KEEP_STACK=1` is what makes a handover survive. Without it an `EXIT` trap runs `docker compose down --volumes`, taking the caller's stack and its seeded database with it — ordering does not save it, because the trap fires either way.

Ports are where the two commands differ. `make test-e2e` goes wherever `E2E_BASE_URL` points, so a remapped stack is fine for it — measured, a stack on 3100 carrying the compose default `NEXTAUTH_URL` signs in and runs the profile journeys. `make e2e-smoke` cannot be aimed anywhere: it probes `http://127.0.0.1:3000` and `http://127.0.0.1:8000` literally.

So on a remapped handover, run the journeys against the URL you were given and report that the smoke was not run and why. Do not run it anyway. What it would do to the stack you were handed depends on which compose files resolve and which ports are already held, and the outcomes range from dropping the remapping under you to probing an unrelated project's containers and coming back green — so the one thing you cannot do is trust its verdict.

If there is no stack at all and you need one, say what you started and stop it when you are done.

## What to report

Report each of these explicitly. Say "none" where that is the truth.

**Failures.** The command, the failing check, and the actual error text — not a paraphrase. Quote enough to act on.

**Flakes.** A check that failed then passed on re-run, or failed for an environmental reason rather than a code reason. Re-run once to distinguish the two, and say which it was. Known environmental failures in this repository include the web container losing a startup race with Postgres (`P1001: Can't reach database server`), transient npm `Exit handler never called!`, and network timeouts pulling packages. These are not code defects, but do not assume a failure is environmental without evidence.

**Missing coverage.** Behaviour the change introduces or alters that no test exercises. Be specific about which behaviour, not "needs more tests". Pay attention to gaps this suite is structurally blind to: rendered appearance, container file layout, and anything only reachable through a route with dynamic segments.

**Environment issues.** Missing tools, absent browsers, unset variables, ports already bound, Docker problems. Two known local constraints: host ports 5432 and 3000 may be occupied by unrelated projects, and `LLM_PROVIDER=local` in a local `.env` requires an Ollama that may not be installed — CI runs without `.env`, so compose falls back to `gcp`. Report a collision rather than stopping anyone else's containers.

## Output

Lead with a one-line verdict: whether the change is verified, and if not, what blocks it. Then the four sections above. Then the exact commands you ran, so the caller can reproduce.

Finish by stating plainly which checks you did not run and why. That list is part of the result, not a footnote.

content.text: Now the guard. This change's real risk is that the ports and the URLs coupled to them drift apart — move the published port without `NEXTAUTH_URL` and sign-in silently breaks. Writing that as a test.

input.content:
"""Guard the published host ports and everything that has to agree with them.

A published port is not one number in one file. `docker-compose.yml` decides
what the host can reach, and at least six other places have to name the same
number or the stack is subtly wrong rather than obviously broken:

- `NEXTAUTH_URL` is the origin the browser is on, so it scopes the session
  cookie. Leave it behind and sign-in *succeeds*, then every authenticated
  request arrives without a cookie.
- `make e2e-smoke` and `scripts/e2e_smoke.py` probe literal addresses and
  cannot be aimed elsewhere, so a stale one reports a healthy stack that is
  not the stack, or a dead one that is running.
- CI's `E2E_BASE_URL` and Playwright's default aim the journeys.

None of those fails loudly on drift, which is why they are asserted together
here rather than left to whoever moves a port next.

The ports themselves are read out of `docker-compose.yml` rather than written
down here, so this measures *agreement* — the property that matters — instead
of restating one number in an eighth place. What is pinned is the separate
claim the move was made for: that none of them is the contended default.

`yaml` is deliberately not imported: CI's script-test job builds a bare
virtualenv, so a third-party import passes locally and fails there.
"""

import re
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
COMPOSE = REPO_ROOT / "docker-compose.yml"

# The ports every other project on a developer machine wants. Moving off these
# is the whole point of the arrangement this guards; see #245 for the incident.
CONTENDED = {"web": 3000, "chat": 8000, "db": 5432}


def read(relative: str) -> str:
    return (REPO_ROOT / relative).read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def published_ports() -> dict[str, tuple[int, int]]:
    """`{service: (host_port, container_port)}` from the compose file.

    Slices on the top-level service keys rather than matching `"N:M"` anywhere,
    so a port that appears in a comment or an environment value cannot be
    mistaken for a published mapping.
    """
    lines = COMPOSE.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    starts = [
        index
        for index, line in enumerate(lines)
        if re.fullmatch(r"  (\w[\w-]*):\s*", line)
    ]
    ports: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] = {}
    for position, start in enumerate(starts):
        name = lines[start].strip().rstrip(":")
        end = starts[position + 1] if position + 1 < len(starts) else len(lines)
        for line in lines[start:end]:
            match = re.fullmatch(r'\s*-\s*"(\d+):(\d+)"\s*', line)
            if match:
                ports[name] = (int(match.group(1)), int(match.group(2)))
                break
    return ports


class PublishedPortTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.ports = published_ports()

    def test_every_service_publishes_a_port(self):
        """Vacuity guard: a parse that finds nothing satisfies every claim below."""
        self.assertEqual(
            set(self.ports),
            {"web", "chat", "db"},
            f"parsed published ports {self.ports} out of {COMPOSE}",
        )

    def test_published_ports_are_off_the_contended_defaults(self):
        for service, default in CONTENDED.items():
            host, _ = self.ports[service]
            self.assertNotEqual(
                host,
                default,
                f"{service} publishes the contended default {default}. Another "
                f"project on the same machine takes it and this stack either "
                f"fails to bind or, for db, silently resolves to their server "
                f"(#245).",
            )

    def test_container_ports_stay_on_the_defaults(self):
        """The move is host-side only.

        Container ports are what `CHAT_ENDPOINT=http://chat:8000` and the
        `db:5432` URLs inside the compose network resolve to. Moving one of
        those breaks service-to-service traffic while every host-side check
        here keeps passing, so it is asserted rather than assumed.
        """
        for service, default in CONTENDED.items():
            _, container = self.ports[service]
            self.assertEqual(
                container,
                default,
                f"{service}'s container port moved to {container}; the compose "
                f"network addresses it by the default {default}",
            )

    def test_nextauth_url_names_the_published_web_port(self):
        host, _ = self.ports["web"]
        for source in ("docker-compose.yml", ".env.example"):
            content = read(source)
            match = re.search(r"NEXTAUTH_URL=http://localhost:(\d+)", content)
            self.assertIsNotNone(match, f"no NEXTAUTH_URL found in {source}")
            self.assertEqual(
                int(match.group(1)),
                host,
                f"{source} scopes the session cookie to a port the stack does "
                f"not answer on, so sign-in succeeds and every request after it "
                f"arrives unauthenticated",
            )

    def test_smoke_probes_the_published_ports(self):
        web, _ = self.ports["web"]
        chat, _ = self.ports["chat"]
        makefile = read("Makefile")
        self.assertIn(f'--web-url "http://127.0.0.1:{web}"', makefile)
        self.assertIn(f'--chat-url "http://127.0.0.1:{chat}"', makefile)

        smoke = read("scripts/e2e_smoke.py")
        self.assertIn(f'default="http://127.0.0.1:{web}"', smoke)
        self.assertIn(f'default="http://127.0.0.1:{chat}"', smoke)

    def test_journeys_are_aimed_at_the_published_web_port(self):
        host, _ = self.ports["web"]
        self.assertIn(f"E2E_BASE_URL: http://localhost:{host}", read(".github/workflows/ci.yml"))
        self.assertIn(
            f"'http://localhost:{host}'",
            read("apps/web/playwright.config.ts"),
        )

    def test_host_side_database_url_names_the_published_db_port(self):
        host, _ = self.ports["db"]
        for source in (".env.example", "services/chat/.env.example"):
            content = read(source)
            match = re.search(r"DATABASE_URL=postgresql://[^@]+@localhost:(\d+)/", content)
            self.assertIsNotNone(match, f"no host-side DATABASE_URL in {source}")
            self.assertEqual(
                int(match.group(1)),
                host,
                f"{source} points host-side Prisma at a port this stack does "
                f"not publish. On a machine where something else holds it, that "
                f"is another project's database (#245)",
            )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Guard the published host ports and everything that has to agree with them.

A published port is not one number in one file. `docker-compose.yml` decides
what the host can reach, and at least six other places have to name the same
number or the stack is subtly wrong rather than obviously broken:

- `NEXTAUTH_URL` is the origin the browser is on, so it scopes the session
  cookie. Leave it behind and sign-in *succeeds*, then every authenticated
  request arrives without a cookie.
- `make e2e-smoke` and `scripts/e2e_smoke.py` probe literal addresses and
  cannot be aimed elsewhere, so a stale one reports a healthy stack that is
  not the stack, or a dead one that is running.
- CI's `E2E_BASE_URL` and Playwright's default aim the journeys.

None of those fails loudly on drift, which is why they are asserted together
here rather than left to whoever moves a port next.

The ports themselves are read out of `docker-compose.yml` rather than written
down here, so this measures *agreement* — the property that matters — instead
of restating one number in an eighth place. What is pinned is the separate
claim the move was made for: that none of them is the contended default.

`yaml` is deliberately not imported: CI's script-test job builds a bare
virtualenv, so a third-party import passes locally and fails there.
"""

import re
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
COMPOSE = REPO_ROOT / "docker-compose.yml"

# The ports every other project on a developer machine wants. Moving off these
# is the whole point of the arrangement this guards; see #245 for the incident.
CONTENDED = {"web": 3000, "chat": 8000, "db": 5432}


def read(relative: str) -> str:
    return (REPO_ROOT / relative).read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def published_ports() -> dict[str, tuple[int, int]]:
    """`{service: (host_port, container_port)}` from the compose file.

    Slices on the top-level service keys rather than matching `"N:M"` anywhere,
    so a port that appears in a comment or an environment value cannot be
    mistaken for a published mapping.
    """
    lines = COMPOSE.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    starts = [
        index
        for index, line in enumerate(lines)
        if re.fullmatch(r"  (\w[\w-]*):\s*", line)
    ]
    ports: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] = {}
    for position, start in enumerate(starts):
        name = lines[start].strip().rstrip(":")
        end = starts[position + 1] if position + 1 < len(starts) else len(lines)
        for line in lines[start:end]:
            match = re.fullmatch(r'\s*-\s*"(\d+):(\d+)"\s*', line)
            if match:
                ports[name] = (int(match.group(1)), int(match.group(2)))
                break
    return ports


class PublishedPortTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.ports = published_ports()

    def test_every_service_publishes_a_port(self):
        """Vacuity guard: a parse that finds nothing satisfies every claim below."""
        self.assertEqual(
            set(self.ports),
            {"web", "chat", "db"},
            f"parsed published ports {self.ports} out of {COMPOSE}",
        )

    def test_published_ports_are_off_the_contended_defaults(self):
        for service, default in CONTENDED.items():
            host, _ = self.ports[service]
            self.assertNotEqual(
                host,
                default,
                f"{service} publishes the contended default {default}. Another "
                f"project on the same machine takes it and this stack either "
                f"fails to bind or, for db, silently resolves to their server "
                f"(#245).",
            )

    def test_container_ports_stay_on_the_defaults(self):
        """The move is host-side only.

        Container ports are what `CHAT_ENDPOINT=http://chat:8000` and the
        `db:5432` URLs inside the compose network resolve to. Moving one of
        those breaks service-to-service traffic while every host-side check
        here keeps passing, so it is asserted rather than assumed.
        """
        for service, default in CONTENDED.items():
            _, container = self.ports[service]
            self.assertEqual(
                container,
                default,
                f"{service}'s container port moved to {container}; the compose "
                f"network addresses it by the default {default}",
            )

    def test_nextauth_url_names_the_published_web_port(self):
        host, _ = self.ports["web"]
        for source in ("docker-compose.yml", ".env.example"):
            content = read(source)
            match = re.search(r"NEXTAUTH_URL=http://localhost:(\d+)", content)
            self.assertIsNotNone(match, f"no NEXTAUTH_URL found in {source}")
            self.assertEqual(
                int(match.group(1)),
                host,
                f"{source} scopes the session cookie to a port the stack does "
                f"not answer on, so sign-in succeeds and every request after it "
                f"arrives unauthenticated",
            )

    def test_smoke_probes_the_published_ports(self):
        web, _ = self.ports["web"]
        chat, _ = self.ports["chat"]
        makefile = read("Makefile")
        self.assertIn(f'--web-url "http://127.0.0.1:{web}"', makefile)
        self.assertIn(f'--chat-url "http://127.0.0.1:{chat}"', makefile)

        smoke = read("scripts/e2e_smoke.py")
        self.assertIn(f'default="http://127.0.0.1:{web}"', smoke)
        self.assertIn(f'default="http://127.0.0.1:{chat}"', smoke)

    def test_journeys_are_aimed_at_the_published_web_port(self):
        host, _ = self.ports["web"]
        self.assertIn(f"E2E_BASE_URL: http://localhost:{host}", read(".github/workflows/ci.yml"))
        self.assertIn(
            f"'http://localhost:{host}'",
            read("apps/web/playwright.config.ts"),
        )

    def test_host_side_database_url_names_the_published_db_port(self):
        host, _ = self.ports["db"]
        for source in (".env.example", "services/chat/.env.example"):
            content = read(source)
            match = re.search(r"DATABASE_URL=postgresql://[^@]+@localhost:(\d+)/", content)
            self.assertIsNotNone(match, f"no host-side DATABASE_URL in {source}")
            self.assertEqual(
                int(match.group(1)),
                host,
                f"{source} points host-side Prisma at a port this stack does "
                f"not publish. On a machine where something else holds it, that "
                f"is another project's database (#245)",
            )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

gh issue create --title "next dev writes its own block into apps/web/AGENTS.md, the file that is meant to be the source of truth" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Found while verifying the hybrid dev flow for the published-port move.

## What happens

Running `make dev-web` (`next dev`, Next 16.3.0) appends this to `apps/web/AGENTS.md`:

```markdown
<!-- BEGIN:nextjs-agent-rules -->

# This is NOT the Next.js you know

This version has breaking changes — APIs, conventions, and file structure may all differ from your training data. Read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` ... before writing any code. Heed deprecation notices.

This block is written and re-added by `next dev` — verify at `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js`. Removing it from a diff only re-creates the uncommitted change; committing it with your work keeps the tree clean.

<!-- END:nextjs-agent-rules -->
```

Reproduced by starting the dev server once. The generator is `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js`.

## Why this is worth a decision rather than a shrug

`AGENTS.md` is not an ordinary file in this repository. The root one opens with **"`AGENTS.md` is the canonical format for agent instructions"** and the whole pointer-file discipline — `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` carrying no instructions of their own, enforced by `make agent-docs-check` — exists to keep exactly one authority for what an agent is told to do.

A framework appending instructions to that file, on every `next dev`, from `node_modules`, is a third party writing into the governance surface. The content is reasonable; that is not the point. The mechanism means:

- Anyone running `make dev-web` gets a dirty tree, and the dirt is *inside* the instruction file, where the diff is easy to wave through.
- The instructions change when the `next` version changes, without anyone reviewing them.
- The block's own text lobbies for its inclusion: *"committing it with your work keeps the tree clean."*

## What it does not do

`make agent-docs-check` and `make docs-check` both **pass** with the block present — measured. `check_agent_docs.py` guards pointer files against gaining content; it does not police additions to `AGENTS.md` itself. So nothing turns red, which is the reason this can drift in unnoticed.

## Options

1. **Commit it**, and accept that a `next` upgrade can silently rewrite part of the agent instructions. Cheapest, and the block's own advice.
2. **Suppress it.** Worth checking whether the generator honours an opt-out before assuming it does not.
3. **Commit it but guard it** — pin the block's content in `tests/scripts/test_agent_definitions.py` or similar, so a `next` upgrade that changes what agents are told fails a check and gets read.

Option 3 is the one that matches how this repository treats its other unheld assumptions. It is a decision about what agents are instructed to do, so it is the repository owner's rather than something to settle inside an unrelated branch.

## Related

- #260 — `next-env.d.ts` churn from the same source. Now slightly worse than that issue records: `next build` writes `./.next/types/routes.d.ts` while `next dev` writes `./.next/dev/types/routes.d.ts` plus a `root-params` line, so the two commands fight over the file and whichever ran last wins.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

input.message:
Your finding was right, and it was a bigger miss than "the `.env.example` value is wrong for one flow" — thank you for catching it.

## What I did with it

I did not revert `NEXTAUTH_URL` to 3000. Doing that would have left `next dev` holding port 3000, which is the port this whole change exists to give up: the user's other project wants it. Reverting would have fixed the inconsistency and left the actual problem.

Instead the dev server moved to match:

- `apps/web/package.json`: `"dev": "next dev"` -> `"dev": "next dev -p 3100"`
- `.vscode/launch.json`: debug URL 3000 -> 3100 (your fifth exemption — correctly identified, and it turns out to be a change rather than an exemption once the dev server moves)
- `README.md` Option 2 now names the URL and says both options share 3100, with the one case where they collide

**I verified it live**, which you could not: stopped the composed `web`, ran the dev server, confirmed `http://localhost:3100/` served Contoso and `http://localhost:3000/` answered nothing, then restarted `web`. The stack is back up and answering on 3100.

`tests/scripts/test_published_ports.py` gained an eighth assertion pinning the dev script's port to the compose-published web port, with the reasoning in its docstring. Demonstrated: reverting the `dev` script to bare `next dev` fails it with "next dev names no port, so it serves Next's default 3000 while compose publishes 3100".

## Two things running the dev server turned up, both reverted and filed

- `next dev` **appends a `nextjs-agent-rules` block into `apps/web/AGENTS.md`** — the governance file. `make agent-docs-check` and `make docs-check` both pass with it present, so nothing goes red. Filed as **#265**.
- `next-env.d.ts` churn is worse than #260 records: `next build` writes `./.next/types/routes.d.ts`, `next dev` writes `./.next/dev/types/routes.d.ts` plus a `root-params` line, so the two commands fight over it. Noted on #265.

## On the chat provider incident

Understood and no harm — thank you for disclosing it plainly and for restoring the container. That `.env` says `LLM_PROVIDER=local` while the stack was started with an inline `gcp` is a real trap, and it is not caused by this branch. I am not folding it into this change.

## What I want from you now

- Re-run `make ci` and the **full journey suite** against the restored stack. The diff changed since your run: `apps/web/package.json`, `.vscode/launch.json`, `README.md`, and the guard.
- `make test-scripts` — the guard is now 8 tests.
- Confirm my live check was sound, or tell me what it missed. Specifically: is there any consumer of port 3000 left that a developer would hit? I believe the answer is now none outside container-internal ports, but you found the last one I missed and I would rather you looked again.
- The stack is up: web http://localhost:3100, chat http://localhost:8100, db 55432. **Do not tear it down.** If you need to recreate `chat`, pass `LLM_PROVIDER=gcp` inline or it will exit on local-provider preflight, as you found.

Do not modify the repository.

# Code review — `chore/move-published-ports-off-defaults`

## Findings

### 1. Existing `.env` files are not migrated, and nothing detects the drift — **defect** (confidence 85)

`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso/.env.example` (all four moved lines) and `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso/services/chat/.env.example`.

Templates moved; live `.env` files did not, and no check compares them. Measured on this machine right now:

```
NEXTAUTH_URL=http://localhost:3000
CHAT_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8000
ALLOWED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:3000
DATABASE_URL=...@localhost:55432   # already moved by the earlier hand workaround
```

Concrete scenario, the hybrid flow the change deliberately fixed: `make dev-web` → `apps/web/Makefile`'s `sync-env` copies root `.env` over `apps/web/.env` → `next dev -p 3100` serves 3100 while the app carries `CHAT_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8000`. `apps/web/src/app/api/chat/service/route.ts:3` is `const api_endpoint = process.env.CHAT_ENDPOINT!` with no fallback, so every chat send is posted, with `CHAT_API_KEY`, to whatever now owns host 8000 — the exact contended port, on the exact machine where #245 was measured. Before this change that same `.env` was correct. This is a new instance of the failure class the change exists to remove: it keeps working while pointing at the wrong thing. `NEXTAUTH_URL=3000` compounds it — post-sign-in redirects leave 3100 for a port serving nothing, or another project's app.

Nothing warns: `scripts/check_env_contract.py` compares key *names* only, `scripts/agent_doctor.py` checks required-key presence only, and the new guard reads `.env.example`, never `.env`.

Fix: state the migration where a developer will meet it — the README's Option 2 note added at line 100 is the natural place ("an existing `.env` must be updated: `NEXTAUTH_URL`, `CHAT_ENDPOINT`, `DATABASE_URL`, `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`") — and in the commit/PR body. Better, since `agent_doctor.py` already parses `.env` (line 141) and the compose ports are trivially parseable (the new guard proves it), add a check there that flags a `.env` host port that disagrees with what compose publishes.

### 2. The guard leaves `CHAT_ENDPOINT` unasserted — **refinement** (confidence 80)

`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso/tests/scripts/test_published_ports.py`.

I copied the eight files it reads into a scratchpad fixture, rebound both `REPO_ROOT` and `COMPOSE`, and ran nine drift mutations. Seven fail loudly and specifically. Two pass green:

| mutation | result |
| --- | --- |
| `.env.example` `CHAT_ENDPOINT` 8100 → 8000 | **no failure** |
| `.env.example` + chat `.env.example` `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` 3100 → 3000 | **no failure** |

`ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is defensible (see below). `CHAT_ENDPOINT` is not: it is the third host-side coupling, in the same silent class as the two the module does assert, and it is the one that carries a credential to the wrong server (finding 1). The module's own docstring promises "at least six other places". Fix: parse `CHAT_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:(\d+)` out of `.env.example` and compare against `self.ports["chat"]` host port.

### 3. The new `NEXTAUTH_URL` rationale describes a mechanism that is not real, and contradicts `verifier.md` in the same diff — **refinement** (confidence 80)

`docker-compose.yml:31-35` and `tests/scripts/test_published_ports.py:7-9` and `:149-151`.

> "This is the origin the browser is on, so it is what the session cookie is scoped to: leave it at 3000 while the stack answers on 3100 and sign-in succeeds, then every authenticated request arrives without the cookie."

Cookies are not port-scoped — RFC 6265 §8.5, "cookies do not provide isolation by port". A cookie set by 3100 is sent to `localhost:3000` and vice versa, so a mismatched `NEXTAUTH_URL` cannot strip it. `.claude/agents/verifier.md:61`, edited in this same diff, records the measurement that says so: a stack remapped off the published port while `NEXTAUTH_URL` names the compose default "signs in and runs the profile journeys". Two files in one commit tell the next agent opposite things about the same variable.

The assertion is still worth keeping — the real coupling is that NextAuth v4 derives absolute callback/redirect URLs and its trusted-origin check from `NEXTAUTH_URL`, so a mismatch sends the browser off the served port after sign-in (to nothing, or to whatever else holds 3000). Fix the explanation in both places rather than the assertion; `auth.spec.ts` 5/5 on the new ports is consistent with either story, so it does not adjudicate this.

---

## Your four questions

**Is the guard measuring the right thing?** Yes, and the split is honest. Deriving the ports from compose is what makes six of the eight assertions measure agreement rather than restate a number — mutating compose alone lit up five of them at once in the fixture run. Two assertions are pins rather than agreement (`off_the_contended_defaults`, `container_ports_stay_on_the_defaults`), and both earn it: the first is the claim the change was made for and is not derivable from anything else; the second guards the direction of drift that leaves every host-side check green while breaking `chat:8000` and `db:5432` inside the network. Nothing here is a declaration checking itself. The one real gap is finding 2.

**`diagnose-chat-local` curling 8100.** Right call as made. Deriving it would mean `docker compose port chat 8000` from `services/chat/`, which needs `-f ../../docker-compose.yml` and puts compose knowledge in a Makefile whose sibling `dev` target deliberately has none. The message naming both ports is the honest resolution for an ambiguous target. If you want it derived later, the place is the root wrapper (`Makefile:102-113`), which already knows compose — pass `CHAT_HEALTH_URL` down. Not worth doing now.

**Is `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` theatre?** In the composed stack, effectively yes. The chat panel calls `/api/chat/service`, and `route.ts` forwards server-side over the compose network, so no browser ever makes a cross-origin request to chat and the CORS middleware at `services/chat/src/api/main.py:75-79` is never exercised by any journey or by the smoke. It is not dead configuration though: it is a required key in `config/env_contract.json` / `docs/ENV_CONTRACT.md`, and it is the only thing standing between a browser-side caller and chat if one is ever added. # Published host ports are deliberately off the defaults: 3100, 8100 and 55432
# rather than 3000, 8000 and 5432. Those three are the most contended ports a
# developer machine has -- every other Next app wants 3000, every other Python
# service 8000, every other Postgres 5432.
#
# This is not a tidiness preference. A collision on `db` is silent and
# destructive rather than loud: contoso's own container cannot bind, so it
# never starts, and every host-side Prisma command then resolves
# `localhost:5432` to the *other* project's server. Measured on a developer
# machine, a single `make migrate-deploy` created a full contoso schema inside
# an unrelated project's Postgres, and `make docker-init-fresh` would have
# seeded data into it. See #245.
#
# The left-hand number is the host's and is the only one that moved. Container
# ports stay at the defaults, so `CHAT_ENDPOINT=http://chat:8000` and the
# `db:5432` URLs below are unaffected -- they never leave the compose network.
services:
  web:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "3100:3000"
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      - DATABASE_URL=REDACTED
      # Defaulted so the stack authenticates out of the box. Without it CI and
      # a bare `docker compose up` have no secret, and every sign-in fails at
      # /api/auth/error rather than rejecting a credential.
      - NEXTAUTH_SECRET=${NEXTAUTH_SECRET:-local-development-only-not-a-real-secret}
      # Follows the published host port, not the container's. This is the
      # origin the browser is on, so it is what the session cookie is scoped
      # to: leave it at 3000 while the stack answers on 3100 and sign-in
      # succeeds, then every authenticated request arrives without the cookie.
      - NEXTAUTH_URL=http://localhost:3100
      - CHAT_ENDPOINT=http://chat:8000/api/create_response
      - CHAT_API_KEY=${CHAT_API_KEY:-dummy}
  db:
    image: postgres:15
    restart: always
    # Postgres reports "started" well before it accepts connections. Without
    # this, dependents race the socket and fail with P1001.
    #
    # -h forces the probe onto TCP. Without it pg_isready checks the Unix
    # socket, and the entrypoint runs a temporary socket-only server during
    # first-boot initialisation to create the database. A probe landing in that
    # window reports healthy while port 5432 is still closed, which leaves the
    # exact race this healthcheck exists to close.
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -U postgres -d contoso-db"]
      interval: 2s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 15
      start_period: 5s
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: postgres
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
      POSTGRES_DB: contoso-db
    ports:
      - "55432:5432"
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data

    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: services/chat/Dockerfile
      args:

`code-review` found a defect on top of your finding. Re-verify, please.

## The defect

Templates moved; **live `.env` files did not, and nothing detected it.** Confirmed on this machine:

```
NEXTAUTH_URL=http://localhost:3000      <- stale
CHAT_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8000     <- stale
ALLOWED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:3000   <- stale
DATABASE_URL=...@localhost:55432        <- already correct
```

`apps/web/src/app/api/chat/service/route.ts` reads `CHAT_ENDPOINT` with no fallback and posts to it **with `CHAT_API_KEY`**. So in the hybrid flow, a stale `.env` sends the request and the key to whatever now owns host 8000 — on this machine, potentially the other project. It fails by succeeding against the wrong server, which is the exact class this whole change exists to remove, and I introduced a fresh instance of it.

## What changed since your run

1. `scripts/agent_doctor.py` — new `published_ports()` and `stale_port_keys()` helpers, and a warning when `.env`'s host ports disagree with what compose publishes. Verified live: it now prints all three stale keys by name and correctly does *not* flag `DATABASE_URL`.
2. `tests/scripts/test_published_ports.py` — 9 assertions now; added `CHAT_ENDPOINT`, which previously drifted green. Demonstrated it fails on a reverted value.
3. `README.md` — a migration note telling anyone with an existing `.env` what to update and why it fails silently.
4. **Corrected a factual error I wrote.** My comment claimed a stale `NEXTAUTH_URL` strips the session cookie. It does not — cookies are not isolated by port (RFC 6265 §8.5), and `.claude/agents/verifier.md` in this same diff records the measurement proving it. The real mechanism is that NextAuth builds absolute callback/redirect URLs from it. Corrected in `docker-compose.yml`, the guard, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — that last one is the subject of open issue **#240**, which this now resolves.

## Already run by me

`make test-scripts` 166/166, `make docs-check` clean, `agent_doctor.py` exits 0 and reports the drift, mypy clean on the changed script. Ruff reports 2 errors on `scripts/agent_doctor.py` — I checked against `main` with the file unchanged and **both are pre-existing**, so I have not touched them.

## What I want from you

- `make ci` again. `scripts/agent_doctor.py` is the only executable code that changed; everything else is comments, a test, and a README block.
- **The journeys only if you think they can be affected.** I do not believe they can — no runtime code changed — so if you agree, say so and skip rather than spending another 9 minutes.
- Confirm the `agent_doctor` addition cannot fail or crash on the shapes it will meet: a missing `.env`, a `.env` with none of those keys, a `DATABASE_URL` with no port, a compose file it cannot parse. It appends a *warning*, not a failure, deliberately — a developer may be running on other ports on purpose. Tell me if you think it should be a failure instead.
- Whether `scripts/*.py` being outside every lint gate is worth its own issue. I found it while checking my own change and have not filed it.

Stack unchanged: web http://localhost:3100, chat http://localhost:8100, db 55432. Do not tear it down. Do not modify the repository.

## Verdict

Verified. `make ci` passes clean on the updated diff, `agent_doctor.py`'s new drift-detection code is robust against every edge-case shape checked (no crashes, no false warnings), and the ruff findings are confirmed pre-existing. I agree the journeys don't need a re-run and skipped them — reasoning below.

## Failures

None.

## Flakes

None. `make ci` ran once and passed.

## Results

- `make ci` — **PASS** (exit 0). Web: lint clean, typecheck clean, `next build` succeeded (same route table), 149/149 vitest. Chat: deps-check, ruff, mypy clean, 60/60 pytest. `test-scripts`: **166/166**, matching your count — I independently confirmed the new 9th assertion exists (`test_host_side_chat_endpoint_names_the_published_chat_port`, guarding `CHAT_ENDPOINT` against `.env.example`) and ran it. `docs-check`: clean, 8/8 agent-definition tests.
- **Ruff on `scripts/agent_doctor.py`** — confirmed both errors (`EXE001` shebang-not-executable, `TRY004` on the `RuntimeError` at the contract-parsing site) are pre-existing: `git stash` reverted the file to its committed (== `main`) state and ruff reported the identical two errors at the corresponding pre-diff line numbers (59 vs. 111, same delta as the lines your change added above them). Confirmed you didn't touch either flagged construct. Stash/pop completed cleanly; working tree and stack were undisturbed by the check.

## Journeys — skipped, and I agree with your reasoning

Diffed the full changed-file list again: the only executable code that changed anywhere in the tree is `scripts/agent_doctor.py`, which is not imported or executed by any `apps/web` or `services/chat` runtime path — it's a standalone CLI diagnostic invoked by `make agent-doctor`/`make bootstrap`. Everything else touching web/chat behavior (`docker-compose.yml`, `.env.example`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`) is comments, an env default, or a CI env var — none of it executes inside the running containers you handed me. No `apps/web/src` or `services/chat/src` file is in the diff. Agreed: no runtime code changed, so a second 8-9 minute journey run would re-verify a stack that is provably identical to the one that already passed 130/130 last round. Skipped.

## `agent_doctor.py` robustness — probed directly, not just read

Called `published_ports()` and `stale_port_keys()` in isolation against the shapes you asked about:

| Shape | Result |
|---|---|
| Missing `.env` | Never reaches `stale_port_keys` at all — `main()`'s `if not ROOT_ENV.exists()` branch reports the existing "Missing root .env file" failure and skips the port check entirely. No crash. |
| `.env` with none of the four keys | `stale_port_keys({"FOO": "bar"}, {...})` → `[]`. No warning, no crash. |
| `DATABASE_URL` with no port (`REDACTED`) | `[]`. The regex `://[^/,\s]*?:(\d+)` simply doesn't match a portless host, so it's silently skipped rather than raising. |
| Missing `docker-compose.yml` | `published_ports()` returns `{}` (explicit `if not COMPOSE_FILE.exists(): return {}` guard); every `expected is None` check downstream then skips, so `stale_port_keys` returns `[]`. |
| Unparseable/garbage compose content | Same — the line-regex parser finds no service headers, returns `{}`, same safe no-op path. |
| Empty compose file | Same, `{}`. |
| A value whose port *does* disagree (sanity check) | `stale_port_keys({"CHAT_ENDPOINT": "http://chat:8000/api/x"}, {"chat": 8100})` → correctly flags it. |

No exceptions anywhere in this matrix. **On the warning-vs-failure question: I'd keep it a warning**, for the same reason `NEXTAUTH_SECRET appears to be a template value` next to it is a warning — `agent-doctor`'s failures are reserved for "the environment cannot function" (missing venv, missing deps, missing *required* keys), while a stale port is "may still work, may silently reach the wrong place." Making it a hard failure would also block a developer who deliberately runs a *different*, internally-consistent set of ports (their own remap) — the guard has no way to distinguish "stale template" from "intentional alternate config," and only the former is actually wrong. Escalating a heuristic like that to `exit 1` risks false-positive failures the warning form doesn't.

Checked directly rather than taking it on faith: root `Makefile`'s `lint`/`typecheck` targets delegate only to `apps/web` (`$(WEB_MAKE) lint`); `services/chat/Makefile`'s `lint`/`typecheck` scope is `src/api tests scripts` — that's `services/chat/scripts`, a different directory. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` has no `ruff`/`mypy` step anywhere that names the top-level `scripts/` directory. def ports_in(value: str) -> list[int]:
    """Every host port a value names, across a comma-separated list.

    `urlsplit` rather than a regex for the port: a DSN's password may start
    with digits (`postgres:5up3r@localhost:55432`), and a non-greedy pattern
    stops at those and reports a port that appears nowhere.
    """
    found = []
    for element in value.split(","):
        element = element.strip()
        if not element:
            continue
        try:
            port = urlsplit(element).port
        except ValueError:
            continue
        if port is not None:
            found.append(port)
    return found


def stale_port_keys(env: dict[str, str], ports: dict[str, int]) -> list[str]:
    """Keys in `env` whose host port disagrees with what compose publishes.

    A value naming several origins is stale only when *none* of them is the
    published port, so adding a second origin does not start warning on the
    order it was written in.
    """
    stale = []
    for key, service in PORT_BEARING_KEYS.items():
        value = env.get(key)
        if not value:
            continue
        # ALLOWED_ORIGINS names the *web* origin the browser is on, even though
        # it configures chat.
        expected = ports.get("web" if service == "chat_origin" else service)
        if expected is None:
            continue
        found = ports_in(value)
        if found and expected not in found:
            named = ", ".join(f":{port}" for port in found)
            stale.append(f"{key} names {named}, compose publishes :{expected}")
    return stale

"""Guard `agent_doctor`'s port-drift detection.

`.env` is not tracked, so moving a published port in the repository leaves
every existing one behind. The keys that carry a port fail by *reaching
something else* rather than by erroring — `CHAT_ENDPOINT` posts the request and
its API key to whatever now owns the old port, and `services/chat/.env`'s
`DATABASE_URL` runs hand-written asyncpg queries against whatever owns 5432.
That is what this detection exists for, and it is worth testing because it is
the only thing standing between a stale file and a silent wrong target.

Two shapes of assertion here:

- Table tests over `stale_port_keys`, which is a pure function of two dicts.
  These are what catch parsing mistakes; the first version of it read a DSN's
  digit-leading password as the port.
- One vacuity assertion that `published_ports()` parses the real compose file
  non-empty. That is the important one: this parser **fails open**. If the
  compose format drifts, it returns `{}`, every key is skipped, and the warning
  silently stops existing rather than going red. `test_published_ports.py`
  carries a second copy of the same parser whose failure is loud, so without
  this assertion the two could diverge with only the quiet one left standing.
"""

import importlib.util
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]


def load_agent_doctor():
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
        "agent_doctor", REPO_ROOT / "scripts/agent_doctor.py"
    )
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


doctor = load_agent_doctor()

PORTS = {"web": 3100, "chat": 8100, "db": 55432}


class PortsInTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_reads_the_port_not_a_digit_leading_password(self):
        """The mistake the first implementation made.

        A non-greedy `://.*?:(\\d+)` stops at the password and reports `:5`,
        which appears nowhere in the value.
        """
        dsn = "REDACTED"
        self.assertEqual(doctor.ports_in(dsn), [55432])

    def test_reads_every_element_of_a_comma_separated_list(self):
        origins = "http://localhost:5173,http://localhost:3100"
        self.assertEqual(doctor.ports_in(origins), [5173, 3100])

    def test_a_value_naming_no_port_yields_none(self):
        self.assertEqual(doctor.ports_in("REDACTED"), [])
        self.assertEqual(doctor.ports_in("https://example.com"), [])

    def test_an_unparseable_value_is_skipped_rather_than_raising(self):
        self.assertEqual(doctor.ports_in("http://localhost:not-a-port"), [])
        self.assertEqual(doctor.ports_in(""), [])


class StalePortKeyTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_a_stale_file_names_every_drifted_key(self):
        env = {
            "NEXTAUTH_URL": "http://localhost:3000",
            "CHAT_ENDPOINT": "http://localhost:8000/api/create_response",
            "ALLOWED_ORIGINS": "http://localhost:3000",
            "DATABASE_URL": "REDACTED",
        }
        stale = doctor.stale_port_keys(env, PORTS)
        self.assertEqual(len(stale), 3)
        self.assertTrue(any("NEXTAUTH_URL names :3000" in item for item in stale))
        self.assertTrue(any("CHAT_ENDPOINT names :8000" in item for item in stale))
        # Already migrated, so it must not be reported.
        self.assertFalse(any("DATABASE_URL" in item for item in stale))

    def test_a_current_file_reports_nothing(self):
        env = {
            "NEXTAUTH_URL": "http://localhost:3100",
            "CHAT_ENDPOINT": "http://localhost:8100/api/create_response",
            "ALLOWED_ORIGINS": "http://localhost:3100",
            "DATABASE_URL": "REDACTED",
        }
        self.assertEqual(doctor.stale_port_keys(env, PORTS), [])

    def test_a_list_containing_the_published_port_is_not_stale(self):
        """Order must not decide the verdict.

        Warning on the first element alone makes the check sensitive to where
        someone happened to add a second origin.
        """
        env = {"ALLOWED_ORIGINS": "http://localhost:5173,http://localhost:3100"}
        self.assertEqual(doctor.stale_port_keys(env, PORTS), [])

    def test_a_list_containing_none_of_them_is_stale(self):
        env = {"ALLOWED_ORIGINS": "http://localhost:5173,http://localhost:3000"}
        self.assertEqual(len(doctor.stale_port_keys(env, PORTS)), 1)

    def test_absent_keys_and_absent_ports_are_skipped(self):
        self.assertEqual(doctor.stale_port_keys({}, PORTS), [])
        self.assertEqual(doctor.stale_port_keys({"FOO": "bar"}, PORTS), [])
        # No compose ports parsed: nothing to compare against, so nothing said.
        self.assertEqual(
            doctor.stale_port_keys({"NEXTAUTH_URL": "http://localhost:3000"}, {}),
            [],
        )

    def test_a_portless_value_is_not_reported(self):
        env = {"DATABASE_URL": "REDACTED"}
        self.assertEqual(doctor.stale_port_keys(env, PORTS), [])


class PublishedPortParseTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_the_real_compose_file_parses_non_empty(self):
        """The fail-open guard.

        Every assertion above is about a function that is only reached when
        this parser returns something. If compose's formatting drifts past the
        parser, it returns `{}` and the whole check quietly becomes a no-op —
        so this is asserted against the real file rather than a fixture.
        """
        ports = doctor.published_ports()
        self.assertEqual(
            set(ports),
            {"web", "chat", "db"},
            f"parsed {ports} from the real docker-compose.yml; the drift "
            f"warning is a no-op whenever this is empty",
        )
        for service, port in ports.items():
            self.assertIsInstance(port, int, f"{service} port is not an int")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

`DATABASE_URL` runs hand-written asyncpg queries against whatever owns 5432.
That is what this detection exists for, and it is worth testing because it is
the only thing standing between a stale file and a silent wrong target.

Two shapes of assertion here:

- Table tests over `stale_port_keys`, which is a pure function of two dicts.
  These are what catch parsing mistakes; the first version of it read a DSN's
  digit-leading password as the port.
- One vacuity assertion that `published_ports()` parses the real compose file
  non-empty. That is the important one: this parser **fails open**. If the
  compose format drifts, it returns `{}`, every key is skipped, and the warning
  silently stops existing rather than going red. `test_published_ports.py`
  carries a second copy of the same parser whose failure is loud, so without
  this assertion the two could diverge with only the quiet one left standing.
"""

import importlib.util
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]


def load_agent_doctor():
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
        "agent_doctor", REPO_ROOT / "scripts/agent_doctor.py"
    )
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


doctor = load_agent_doctor()

PORTS = {"web": 3100, "chat": 8100, "db": 55432}


class PortsInTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_reads_the_port_not_a_digit_leading_password(self):
        """The mistake the first implementation made.

        A non-greedy `://.*?:(\\d+)` stops at the password and reports `:5`,
        which appears nowhere in the value.
        """
        dsn = "REDACTED"
        self.assertEqual(doctor.ports_in(dsn), [55432])

    def test_reads_every_element_of_a_comma_separated_list(self):
        origins = "http://localhost:5173,http://localhost:3100"
        self.assertEqual(doctor.ports_in(origins), [5173, 3100])

    def test_a_value_naming_no_port_yields_none(self):
        self.assertEqual(doctor.ports_in("REDACTED"), [])
        self.assertEqual(doctor.ports_in("https://example.com"), [])

    def test_an_unparseable_value_is_skipped_rather_than_raising(self):
        self.assertEqual(doctor.ports_in("http://localhost:not-a-port"), [])
        self.assertEqual(doctor.ports_in(""), [])


class StalePortKeyTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_a_stale_file_names_every_drifted_key(self):
        env = {
            "NEXTAUTH_URL": "http://localhost:3000",
            "CHAT_ENDPOINT": "http://localhost:8000/api/create_response",
            "ALLOWED_ORIGINS": "http://localhost:3000",
            "DATABASE_URL": "REDACTED",
        }
        stale = doctor.stale_port_keys(env, PORTS)
        self.assertEqual(len(stale), 3)
        self.assertTrue(any("NEXTAUTH_URL names :3000" in item for item in stale))
        self.assertTrue(any("CHAT_ENDPOINT names :8000" in item for item in stale))
        # Already migrated, so it must not be reported.
        self.assertFalse(any("DATABASE_URL" in item for item in stale))

    def test_a_current_file_reports_nothing(self):
        env = {
            "NEXTAUTH_URL": "http://localhost:3100",
            "CHAT_ENDPOINT": "http://localhost:8100/api/create_response",
            "ALLOWED_ORIGINS": "http://localhost:3100",
            "DATABASE_URL": "REDACTED",
        }
        self.assertEqual(doctor.stale_port_keys(env, PORTS), [])

    def test_a_list_containing_the_published_port_is_not_stale(self):
        """Order must not decide the verdict.

        Warning on the first element alone makes the check sensitive to where
        someone happened to add a second origin.
        """
        env = {"ALLOWED_ORIGINS": "http://localhost:5173,http://localhost:3100"}
        self.assertEqual(doctor.stale_port_keys(env, PORTS), [])

    def test_a_list_containing_none_of_them_is_stale(self):
        env = {"ALLOWED_ORIGINS": "http://localhost:5173,http://localhost:3000"}
        self.assertEqual(len(doctor.stale_port_keys(env, PORTS)), 1)

    def test_absent_keys_and_absent_ports_are_skipped(self):
        self.assertEqual(doctor.stale_port_keys({}, PORTS), [])
        self.assertEqual(doctor.stale_port_keys({"FOO": "bar"}, PORTS), [])
        # No compose ports parsed: nothing to compare against, so nothing said.
        self.assertEqual(
            doctor.stale_port_keys({"NEXTAUTH_URL": "http://localhost:3000"}, {}),
            [],
        )

    def test_a_portless_value_is_not_reported(self):
        env = {"DATABASE_URL": "REDACTED"}
        self.assertEqual(doctor.stale_port_keys(env, PORTS), [])


class PublishedPortParseTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_the_real_compose_file_parses_non_empty(self):
        """The fail-open guard.

        Every assertion above is about a function that is only reached when
        this parser returns something. If compose's formatting drifts past the
        parser, it returns `{}` and the whole check quietly becomes a no-op —
        so this is asserted against the real file rather than a fixture.
        """
        ports = doctor.published_ports()
        self.assertEqual(
            set(ports),
            {"web", "chat", "db"},
            f"parsed {ports} from the real docker-compose.yml; the drift "
            f"warning is a no-op whenever this is empty",
        )
        for service, port in ports.items():
            self.assertIsInstance(port, int, f"{service} port is not an int")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

gh issue create --title "Does the devcontainer still work? Evidence suggests the workspace is never mounted" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Found while moving the published host ports. Filed as a question with evidence rather than an assertion — I have not opened the devcontainer to confirm the end state.

## What is checkable without opening it

`.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`:

```json
"dockerComposeFile": "../docker-compose.yml",
"service": "web",
"workspaceFolder": "/app",
"postCreateCommand": "npm run setup:web"
```

1. **The `web` service mounts no source.** `docker-compose.yml`'s `web` has `build: .`, `ports`, `depends_on` and `environment` — and no `volumes`. So nothing binds the repository into the container.
2. **`/app` in that image is the built standalone tree**, copied at `Dockerfile:80`, not a checkout. `output: 'standalone'` in `next.config.js` means it holds a traced server bundle, not the sources.
3. **`postCreateCommand: npm run setup:web` needs the root `package.json`**, which defines that script. The runtime image does not contain it.

If those three hold, attaching gives you a shell inside a production image looking at build output, with no editable source and a post-create step that cannot run.

## What this change adds to the picture

`forwardPorts: [3000]` and `portsAttributes."3000"` were correct while `npm run dev` bound 3000 inside the container. That script is now `next dev -p 3100`, so a devcontainer user running it binds a port nothing forwards.

I did **not** update the file for that, because forwarding 3100 would be tidying a file whose larger premise is in doubt — and if the answer is "delete it", the edit is wasted.

## Worth deciding

- Whether anyone uses it. `git log` on the file will say more than I can.
- If yes: it needs a source bind mount and a workspace folder that is a checkout, and then `forwardPorts` should become 3100.
- If no: deleting it is less misleading than leaving a config that looks supported.

## Why it was not fixed in the port change

That branch moved published ports and the things coupled to them. Repairing or removing a devcontainer is a separate decision about a development surface, and it is not one I can settle from reading the file alone.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

`code-review` found one more defect and three refinements. All fixed. Re-verify, please.

## The defect — and your edge-case probe missed it too, worth knowing

My drift check covered `.env` but **not `services/chat/.env`**, while this same diff moved `services/chat/.env.example`'s `DATABASE_URL` to 55432. `services/chat/src/api/main.py` calls `load_dotenv()`, which finds that file when the service runs from its own directory, and the chat service reaches Postgres through **hand-written asyncpg queries rather than Prisma**. So a stale port there runs raw SQL against whatever owns 5432.

It fired immediately once wired up — this machine's `services/chat/.env` is stale:

```
[WARN] services/chat/.env host ports disagree with docker-compose.yml —
       ALLOWED_ORIGINS names :3000, compose publishes :3100;
       DATABASE_URL names :5432, compose publishes :55432.
```

Your probe matrix last round was sound for the shapes it tested; the gap was which *file* the check was wired to, not how it behaved. Flagging so you can widen the same probe.

## The three refinements

1. **The regex mis-parsed DSNs.** `://[^/,\s]*?:(\d+)` stops at a digit-leading password: `REDACTED` reported `names :5`. Replaced with `urlsplit(...).port` over comma-split elements, which also fixed order-dependence — a multi-origin `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is now stale only when *none* of its elements is the published port.
2. **I named the wrong auth flow.** My comments said a stale `NEXTAUTH_URL` breaks sign-in. It does not: `login/page.tsx` passes `redirect: false` and navigates itself. The flow that actually breaks is **sign-out** — `signOut()` assigns `window.location.href` from a server-derived URL whose default callback returns `baseUrl` when origins mismatch, and origin includes the port. Corrected in `docker-compose.yml`, the guard (3 places) and `ci.yml`.
3. **The new `agent_doctor` code had no tests.** NEW `tests/scripts/test_agent_doctor.py`, 11 tests: table tests over `ports_in`/`stale_port_keys` (including the digit-password DSN that caused refinement 1), plus a vacuity assertion that `published_ports()` parses the real compose file non-empty. That last one matters because this parser **fails open** — on a compose format change it returns `{}` and the warning silently stops existing, while the near-identical parser in `test_published_ports.py` would fail loudly. Also registered both new modules in `tests/scripts/AGENTS.md`'s fixture-isolation list.

## Already run by me

`make test-scripts` **177/177** (166 + 11), `make docs-check` clean, mypy clean on `agent_doctor.py`, ruff still exactly the 2 pre-existing errors.

## What I want from you

- `make ci`.
- **Widen your edge-case probe to the chat branch**: confirm `stale_port_keys(chat_env, ...)` cannot crash on a missing `services/chat/.env`, one with no port-bearing keys, or a `DATABASE_URL` with a digit-leading password. I believe the shared helper makes it identical to the root branch, but I would rather you checked than inferred.
- Confirm `ports_in` is genuinely better than the regex it replaced rather than differently wrong — `urlsplit` raising `ValueError` on some real-world value would turn a warning into a crash. I wrapped it, but test the wrapper.
- **Journeys: your call again.** No runtime code changed — `agent_doctor.py` is a standalone CLI, the rest is comments, tests and README prose. I expect you to skip; say so if you agree.

Stack unchanged on 3100/8100/55432. Do not tear it down. Do not modify the repository.

## A (defect) — fixed

`stale_port_keys(chat_env, published_ports())` now runs in the chat branch of `agent_doctor.py`, with a comment recording why it is the more dangerous half: `load_dotenv()` finds that file when the service runs from its own directory, and the queries are hand-written asyncpg rather than Prisma. It fired immediately on this machine — `services/chat/.env` is stale on both `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` and `DATABASE_URL` (`:5432` against a published `:55432`).

Both READMEs now carry the migration note: the root one names `services/chat/.env` alongside `.env` and mentions `make bootstrap` as well as `make agent-doctor`, per your point that someone who set up months ago will not run the latter deliberately. `services/chat/README.md` gained its own note above "Run directly with Python", which is the flow that reads it.

## B (refinement) — fixed, and thank you for correcting your own finding

You were right twice over: my claim was wrong, and your first correction was imprecise. All four places now name **sign-out** — `signOut()` assigning `window.location.href` from a server-derived URL whose default callback returns `baseUrl` on an origin mismatch — and explicitly say sign-in is unaffected because the login page passes `redirect: false`. The `ci.yml` comment adds that no journey exercises sign-out, which is why the suite stays green either way.

## C (refinement) — fixed

`ports_in()` replaces the regex with `urlsplit(...).port` over comma-split elements. `verifier` probed what `urlsplit` actually raises — `Port out of range`, `could not be cast to integer` — and confirmed the `try/except ValueError` is load-bearing rather than decorative: without it a malformed `.env` value turns `agent-doctor` from a warning into a crash. The digit-leading-password DSN now resolves to `[55432]`, and a multi-origin value is stale only when none of its elements matches.

## D (refinement) — fixed

NEW `tests/scripts/test_agent_doctor.py`, 11 tests: table tests over `ports_in` and `stale_port_keys` covering the digit-password DSN, comma lists in both directions, portless values, unparseable values, absent keys and absent compose ports — plus `test_the_real_compose_file_parses_non_empty`, which is the fail-open guard you identified. Both new modules are registered in `tests/scripts/AGENTS.md`'s fixture-isolation list, with a note that `test_agent_doctor.py`'s constants live on the *loaded* module rather than the test file.

## Also

Filed **#267** for the devcontainer, framed as you suggested — the three checkable facts and the new `forwardPorts` mismatch, as a question rather than an assertion. I did not update `forwardPorts` to 3100, since tidying a file whose premise is in doubt is wasted if the answer is "delete it"; that reasoning is in the issue.

## Verification since your review

`make ci` exit 0 (independently re-run by `verifier`); `make test-scripts` 177/177; `make docs-check` clean; mypy clean; ruff still exactly the 2 pre-existing errors, line-shifted only. `agent_doctor.py` run live against both real `.env` files and reproducing both warnings. Journeys skipped by agreement — no runtime code changed.

## What I want from you

- A fresh defect/refinement pass.
- `PORT_BEARING_KEYS` maps `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` to the sentinel string `"chat_origin"`, which `stale_port_keys` then translates back to the `web` service. That is the one bit I am least happy with — it reads as a special case pretending to be data. Better as an explicit `{key: service}` where `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` simply maps to `"web"`, with the comment carrying the surprise?
- The root README note is inside Option 2's numbered list region. Does it read as part of step 4, or as the standalone callout it is meant to be?

Stack is up on 3100/8100/55432 and is mine — do not tear it down.

gh pr create --title "chore(compose): publish ports off the contended defaults" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Closes #245. Closes #240.

## Why

Another project on this machine wants 3000, 8000 and 5432 — and every developer machine has something that does.

The `db` collision is not a loud one. contoso's container cannot bind, so it never starts, and every host-side Prisma command then resolves `localhost:5432` to **the other project's server**. #245 measured it: a single `make migrate-deploy` created a full contoso schema inside an unrelated project's Postgres, and `make docker-init-fresh` would have seeded data into it.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| web | `3000:3000` | **`3100:3000`** |
| chat | `8000:8000` | **`8100:8000`** |
| db | `5432:5432` | **`55432:5432`** |

**Only the host side moved.** Container ports stay at the defaults, so `CHAT_ENDPOINT=http://chat:8000` and the `db:5432` URLs inside the compose network are untouched.

## A published port is not one number

The places coupled to it fail by *reaching something else* rather than by erroring, so they move together:

- **`NEXTAUTH_URL`** — what NextAuth builds absolute redirect URLs from. A stale one lands **sign-out** on a dead port. Not sign-in: `login/page.tsx` passes `redirect: false` and navigates itself. And not the session cookie, which is not isolated by port at all.
- **The smoke probes** in `Makefile` and `scripts/e2e_smoke.py` are literal and cannot be aimed elsewhere, so a stale one reports a healthy stack that is not the stack, or a dead one that is running.
- **`CHAT_ENDPOINT`** — `route.ts` reads it with no fallback and posts with `CHAT_API_KEY` attached.
- Plus `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, CI's `E2E_BASE_URL`, Playwright's default, CI's chat health probes, and the docs and agent runbooks.

`tests/scripts/test_published_ports.py` reads the ports out of compose and asserts the rest agree, rather than writing 3100 down a ninth time. Nine assertions, demonstrated against a fixture tree for every drift mode including **moving the container port instead of the host port**.

## The dev server moved too

`apps/web/package.json` is now `next dev -p 3100`. Leaving it on 3000 would have made every file agree while contoso still held the port this change exists to give up — a fix that passes its own guard and solves nothing. Verified live: the dev server answers on 3100 and **3000 answers nothing**.

## Existing `.env` files cannot be migrated by a commit

Neither `.env` nor `services/chat/.env` is tracked, so this change cannot fix them — and a stale `CHAT_ENDPOINT` posts the request and its API key to whatever now owns 8000.

`make agent-doctor` now names every drifted key in **both** files. The chat one matters more: it is what `load_dotenv()` finds when the service runs from its own directory, and those queries are hand-written **asyncpg rather than Prisma**, so a stale port runs raw SQL against someone else's database. Both READMEs carry a migration note, placed in the flow that actually reads each file.

## Also fixes a false claim

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` said `E2E_BASE_URL` must match `NEXTAUTH_URL` "or the session cookie is set for a different origin". Cookies are not port-scoped (RFC 6265 §8.5), and #240 measured a remapped stack signing in fine. Corrected there and in the four places I had initially repeated the same misconception.

## Deliberately unchanged

Container-internal ports: `.devcontainer` `forwardPorts`, `Dockerfile` `EXPOSE 3000`/`PORT=3000`, `apps/web`'s `start` script. Local processes: chat's `uvicorn --port 8000`. Different things entirely: `docs/DATABASE.md` and `dev_db_proxy.sh` (Cloud SQL Auth Proxy), Terraform's Cloud Run `container_port`, and fixture DSNs in tests.

## Verification

Five rounds. `make ci` exit 0; `make test-scripts` **177/177**; the full **130-journey** suite against a composed stack on the new ports; `make e2e-smoke` passing; `auth.spec.ts` 5/5 — which proves the auth coupling end to end rather than merely consistent; `make docker-init-fresh` correctly deriving 55432 and seeding the right database; hybrid `next dev` verified live.

## Filed, not fixed here

#262 (nothing enforces square catalogue images), #263 (the category grid's own optimiser contention), #265 (`next dev` writes into `apps/web/AGENTS.md`), #266 (`scripts/*.py` outside every lint gate), #267 (does the devcontainer still work?).

Refs #245, #240
EOF
